correctness.rationale: The 27 blowup line classes generate rank-seven Picard, and all 45 tritangents have primitive anticanonical class. The inverse image of its rank-one sublattice has rank 21. The exact 21x21 tritangent minor is -1, identifying the primitive lattice. All 120 Steiner nine-line supports are three disjoint tritangent supports and have class 3(-K); their selected 21x21 minor is +3 on the same coordinate rows. Thus the Steiner columns generate a sublattice of index at most three. The coefficient of -K modulo three is surjective on the tritangent lattice, vanishes on Steiner supports, and supplies the matching lower bound. Hence the image is exactly the inverse image of 3Z(-K), and the cokernel is Z^6 plus Z/3. All determinant and enumeration checks were executed from the attached standalone source using exact integers; a separate exact SymPy Smith reduction agreed.

value.rationale: The nine-line union of a Steiner trihedral pair is a natural geometric marking on every smooth cubic surface. The integer question of which formal line combinations can be reconstructed from these markings is nontrivial and yields a complete, sharp characterization by anticanonical divisibility, not merely rank or congruence necessity. The exact absence of 2-primary torsion is structurally informative because closely related larger incidence maps have substantial even-primary defects; the one order-three obstruction is the only remaining obstruction. This is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a small-field enumeration.
